entries.summary: 1353, die 4. maji, Ecclesia herbipolensis pro reformatione tuitione et conservatione jurium suorum quaedam statuit

entries.english:
In God's name, amen. Let it be evidently clear to all who receive these presents that we, Albert, by the grace of God bishop, Heinrich von Hohenloch, our brother, provost, Heinrich von Reinstein, dean, and the whole chapter of the church of Würzburg, for the reform, protection and preservation of the privileges, liberties, customs and rights of the same church in head and members, against all, and especially against those previously named by us and notorious or notoriously manifest violators of such privileges, liberties, customs and rights, have agreed concordantly in word and deed for ourselves and for all and each adhering or wishing to adhere to us in this matter in the future, and are also inseparably united and bound, further for certain reasonable motives and just causes sufficiently notorious and manifest, to be presented and also disclosed before our superiors, ecclesiastical as well as secular, and others at an opportune place and time, since necessity urges us and ours and our church itself, both in head and members, and unfortunately now threatens; and after many chapter discussions and mature, considered deliberation about it, with the consent, decree and authority of us the bishop also intervening in due manner and by custom, it has been duly decided and ordained capitularly by us, the dean and chapter aforesaid, in the manner and order written below.
First, namely, that the prelates and canons, both capitular and extra-capitular, and also the vicars of our aforesaid church, present as well as future, shall not be required to reside personally in our city of Würzburg or its suburbs after a term to be fixed by the six commissaries named below or the majority of them, without fraud or delay, until it is otherwise ordained by the same six commissaries named below or the majority of them. And that the capitular canons of the said church shall be bound to hold and have a peremptory chapter of our church on each Friday of the four Ember seasons each year, while this ordinance lasts, in our town of Karlstadt. But otherwise not only the capitulars themselves but also extra-capitular canons holding prebends shall receive and have their prebends and offerings in full wherever they reside outside Würzburg and its suburbs; the annual dues or pensions of such offerings shall meanwhile be paid and settled in Karlstadt or in Arnstein or in the town of Ochsenfurt. If any of the canons having an offering or offerings suffers loss or diminution in such offering or offerings on account of the aforesaid, then, while such loss and diminution lasts in the payment of his due, he shall be relieved of it at the discretion of the six commissaries named below, provided that the six commissaries concordantly think it necessarily expedient. Whoever of our absent fellow canons wishes to make personal residence according to the custom of our church shall be thenceforth regarded as present canon of our church. The same shall reside personally for half a year continuously without delay in Karlstadt or in Ochsenfurt or in both without delay.
And the court both of the official of our Würzburg curia and the secular provincial court, and the courts of the archdeacons of our aforesaid church, shall be transferred from Würzburg to Karlstadt within a term to be assigned for it by the six commissaries named below or the majority of them, and held and had there in Karlstadt while this ordinance lasts.
Moreover, whoever of our fellow canons or other fellow clerics holding benefices adhering to us in this matter should at any time withdraw effectively, fraudulently and deceitfully, which God forbid, from the observance of this statute and ordinance of union, shall thereby be and remain suspended from receiving the fruits, rents and profits of his benefices; and if he persists in his transgression, he shall be punished more severely for such guilt until he makes due amends at the discretion of the six commissaries or the majority of them. Whoever is accused of the aforesaid may excuse himself by his oath, and after such an oath he shall be held excused. No one henceforth shall be received or admitted as canon of our church unless he has first sworn a bodily oath on the observance of this statute and ordinance of union.
Further, it has been ordained capitularly by us the chapter aforesaid, with the consent and approval of our aforesaid bishop, that the honourable Heinrich the dean aforesaid, Johannes Schenk von Erbach, archdeacon, Hans von Rosenberg, Engelhard von Bebenburg, Ernst von Ristenhusen and Friedrich von Kastel, capitular canons of our church, all together shall have capitular and full power to add, to supply defects and to declare doubtful cases in matters depending, occurring and arising from the aforesaid.
If, however, and whenever any of the six commissaries happens to be impeded in this matter by weakness or pilgrimage or otherwise for a time, then and as often the impeded one may and shall meanwhile substitute another capitular canon, his confrère from the same Würzburg choir, having a capitular voice.
And if and whenever one of the six commissaries resigns or dies, then and as often the remaining five colleagues, who must for this meet in Karlstadt or in Ochsenfurt and be summoned there, or at least the greater part of those then present, may and shall within eight days take another capitular confrère having a capitular voice from the choir of the resigning or dying one of the aforesaid church of Würzburg who must not refuse it.
Furthermore we, Albert, the bishop aforesaid, have promised in good faith and by these presents pledge to maintain and defend, through ourselves and our officials, who must also promise it within a term to be fixed by the six commissaries aforesaid or the majority of them, under oath of homage, to the dean himself or, in his absence, to another of the six commissaries above, in the place and name of him and of all and each others concerned, and also through our servants inside and outside our fortifications and those of our church, all and each of the prelates and canons aforesaid and other clerics and laymen adhering to us and them in this matter or wishing to adhere or giving aid, counsel or favour, in their persons, benefices, goods and rights, ecclesiastical and secular, without cost and damage to them, against any offenders and molesters of theirs.
Moreover we, Albert, the bishop aforesaid, have duly promised in good faith and by these presents pledge to all and each of the prelates, canons and other clerics concerned in this matter, firmly obliging ourselves to it, that if injury, damage or hindrance is inflicted on the chapter, prelates or canons of our aforesaid church or on other clerics or any persons adhering now or in future to us and our church in this matter, jointly or separately, by reason of such causes or on any pretext arising from them, then we shall make or accept no composition or settlement with such injurers, damagers and hinderers, publicly or secretly, unless first full and due satisfaction has been made for such injury, damage and hindrance to the persons who suffered it or to their heirs or successors, according to their estimation or at least that of the six commissaries for the time being or the majority of them, or at least certainty and fuller provision exist that such satisfaction will be made.
Nevertheless we are also bound, wish and ought to pursue, within a term to be assigned to us by the aforesaid six commissaries or the majority of them, according to the quality of place and time, with both our jurisdictions, ecclesiastical as well as secular, and to constrain with the due censure of both, the violators of the privileges, liberties, customs and rights of our aforesaid church and of its chapter, prelates, canons and other clerics and persons of whom it was said above, all offenders, injurers, damagers and hinderers, to obtain the satisfaction and amends due and fitting in this matter, and to execute irrevocably such judgments and others, or have them carried out, and to allow them to be carried out. And we pledge ourselves firmly to this in good faith under this writing.
The ordinance of the foregoing shall be annulled and cease after the aforesaid six commissaries or at least the majority of them have declared that the ordinance should no longer last.
Finally, since it is not permitted by equity, nor fitting by honesty, nor expedient for public benefit, for members to depart from the head, but all members ought to follow the head, and a part is shameful that does not fit its whole, and what touches all should be approved by all, and what is feared to threaten one after another successively without due cause should deservedly be duly guarded against by all, as the laws attest, we therefore confidently presume that our beloved in Christ, the prelates and canons and other clerical persons and beneficiaries of the other collegiate churches of Würzburg, especially the non-exempt, will effectively assist us and our and their cathedral church of Würzburg aforesaid and adhere faithfully and constantly in the foregoing, after they have been requested by us about it.
In strength and testimony of the foregoing the seals of us the bishop and the chapter aforesaid are appended to these presents.
Given at Würzburg, in the year of the Lord 1353, on the fourth day of the month of May.
